      <title>Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza cleared of using AI to write prize-winning story</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/nov/12/zimbabwean-author-simbarashe-kundizeza-cleared-ai-caine-prize-winning-story</link>
      <description><p>After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’</p><p>The Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, after the prestigious Caine prize for African writers concluded that his entry was “human-written” after a month-long investigation.</p><p>Kundizeza’s story <a href="https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6a4f3fb6a6178e0225b39a4c/t/6a95fffc36f1fc568e02f7fe/1788215293124/3.The+Blue+Fighter.pdf">The Blue Fighter</a>, which charts the declining fortunes of a family after the father invests in fish tanks, was announced as the winner of the £10,000 prize on 6 October.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/nov/12/zimbabwean-author-simbarashe-kundizeza-cleared-ai-caine-prize-winning-story">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/egypt-two-trains-deadly-collision</link>
      <description><p>President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo</p><p>Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.</p><p>The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/egypt-two-trains-deadly-collision">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie</link>
      <description><p>Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families</p><p>The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.</p><p>The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/kenya-starvation-cult-leader-guilty-murder-190-children">found the cult leader guilty</a> of the crimes.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Two skulls likely belonging to enslaved people returned to Brazil after Harvard used them in eugenics studies</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/11/harvard-skulls-repatriated-brazil</link>
      <description><p>Remains believed to have belonged to Africans or Afro-Brazilians repatriated after being flown back by diplomats </p><p>Two skulls, including that of a man believed to have taken part in Brazil’s greatest slave revolt but whose remains were taken to the United States and used in racist eugenics studies at Harvard University, were repatriated on Wednesday.</p><p>The remains had been outside Brazil since the 19th century. One was taken about 190 years ago from Salvador, the capital of the state of Bahia; the other, about 160 years ago, from Rio de Janeiro – and were welcomed back in moving, subdued ceremonies in both cities.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/11/harvard-skulls-repatriated-brazil">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/11/red-brigades-leonardo-bertulazzi-escapes-house-arrest-argentina</link>
      <description><p>Leonardo Bertulazzi, 74, awaiting extradition to Italy, reportedly used harness to flee custody</p><p>A 74-year-old former member of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/italy">Italy</a>’s radical Marxist group the Red Brigades has escaped from house arrest in <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/argentina">Argentina</a>, the country’s security ministry confirmed on Wednesday, after he reportedly hid his ankle monitor inside a tube of pork and lowered himself from a fifth-floor balcony.</p><p>Authorities placed Leonardo Bertulazzi under house arrest in Buenos Aires in 2024, prior to his extradition to Italy to serve a 27-year prison sentence.       <description><p>Lawyer says Britain wrong to believe in historic doctrine that crown has sovereignty over parts of oceans</p><p>Britain should not be permitted to act as a 17th-century colonial power treating the waters around the Falkland Islands as a <em>Dominium maris Britannici</em>, Argentina has told an international tribunal.</p><p>Marcelo Kohen, representing Argentina at a hearing in Hamburg, mocked Britain for apparently believing in the historic doctrine that the British crown has sovereignty over expansive parts of the oceans.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/nov/11/argentine-lawyer-mocks-uk-sovereignty-claim-in-falklands-oil-case">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/12/thursday-briefing-what-we-do-and-dont-know-about-alice-huang-and-the-nvidia-affair</link>
      <description><p>In today’s newsletter: US intelligence reportedly believes the former tech executive was recruited by Beijing, raising questions about the security of the AI industry and Trump’s close ties to Nvidia chief Jensen Huang</p><p></p><p>Good morning. Espionage is supposed to be a secretive business, and spies are supposed to be virtually invisible. That hasn’t been the case for Alice Huang, the mysterious Shanghai executive who formed a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang, the founder of Nvidia, one of America’s most powerful tech companies.</p><p>Many questions have arisen since it emerged that US intelligence believes that Huang (no relation of Jensen’s) is an asset recruited by the Chinese intelligence services to spy on behalf of Beijing. This morning’s newsletter explains what we know about the story, and what it tells us about the effectiveness of Chinese espionage. That’s after the headlines.</p><p><em><strong>UK </strong></em>| Ministers are considering <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/media/2026/nov/11/tv-entertainment-industry-protect-women-david-walliams-allegations-nandy">changing the law</a> to force the entertainment industry to better protect women and children in the wake of the revelations over David Walliams and the conviction of Russell Brand.</p><p><em><strong>Climate </strong></em>| The UK government has <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/11/uk-appoints-worlds-first-special-representative-for-climate-security">appointed the world’s first </a>special representative for climate security, in the strongest sign yet of fears that climate breakdown will bring chaos to the country.</p><p><em><strong>US midterms </strong></em>| Democrat Scott Colom has become the first Black senator in Mississippi to be elected since Reconstruction,<a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/11/scott-colom-mississippi-senate-race"> in a stunning upset </a>after more than a week of vote counting in one of the country’s most reliably red states.</p><p><em><strong>Europe </strong></em>| Millions of people across Spain have joined the country’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/11/spain-general-strike-housing-costs">first general strike in 14 years</a>, setting up picket lines to protest against soaring housing prices before an election in which the far right could be catapulted into power.</p><p><em><strong>Technology </strong></em>| Police officers <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/12/facial-recognition-errors-put-ethnic-minorities-at-risk-of-wrongful-arrest-police-watchdog-warns">risk arresting innocent people</a>, especially from ethnic minorities, if they treat inaccurate facial recognition data as evidence, an official report has found.</p> <a       <description><p>Former US secretary of state says most nations are ‘stumbling along’ while Beijing has ‘hugely accelerated’</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/live/2026/nov/10/cop31-live-fossil-fuel-carbon-emissions-climate-crisis-latest-news-updates">Cop31 live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>China is leading the world <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/feb/05/china-green-energy-sector-investment-growth">in moving away from fossil fuels</a>, and the rest of the globe – including the US – must now follow, the former US secretary of state John Kerry has told the Guardian, as Cop watchers wonder exactly how China is going to approach this year’s climate summit.</p><p>As Cop31 opens – this year the climate conference is in Turkey – there is plenty of speculation about whether China will finally step into the leadership role that it has long avoided.       <description><p>Hardline remarks come as Ukrainian military faces disruptions to Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite service</p><p>Vladimir Putin warned US negotiators that Russia would target any foreign troops deployed to Ukraine, in a series of hardline remarks that came as the Ukrainian military faced renewed disruptions to Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite service.</p><p>During the talks at the Kremlin with US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on Thursday, the Russian president refused to soften his territorial demands, insisting on full control over four Ukrainian regions that Moscow claims to have annexed.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/12/vladimir-putin-russia-target-foreign-troops-ukraine-elon-musk-starlink">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Finland bars Russian athletes from entering country over Ukraine war</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/nov/12/finland-bars-russian-athletes-ukraine</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Russians ‘have no business’ in country, says minister</p></li><li><p>Skating and cross-country skiing first to be affected</p></li></ul><p>Finland says it will restrict entry to the country for Russian athletes because of the war in Ukraine, potentially affecting a number of winter sports. The move follows a backlash in Finland to Russia being reinstated for the ice hockey world championships.</p><p>“As long as Russia’s war of aggression continues, Russian athletes have no business in Finland,” said Elina Valtonen, the Minister for Foreign Affairs. “Their entry into the country would be a threat to Finland’s international relations. The same is true of other short-term work under visas that is not essential to Finland’s national interests.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/nov/12/finland-bars-russian-athletes-ukraine">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>‘Rules of origin’ on vehicle batteries due to come into force on 1 January if deal on new delay is not reached</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/live/2026/nov/12/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-affairs-share-price-plunges-live-latest">Business live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>The UK car industry is preparing to push for a two-year delay to Brexit tariffs on electric cars traded with the EU, after an initial European proposal suggested a shorter delay.</p><p>Tariffs are due to kick in on 1 January for the majority of electric cars traded between the EU and UK unless the two sides can come to an agreement to delay for a second time the implementation of “rules of origin” on batteries.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/12/uk-car-industry-rules-of-origin-brexit-ev-tariffs-eu">Continue reading...</a></description>

France will seek European-level sanctions against Iran in response to cyberattacks on hundreds of supermarket fridges, Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Tuesday, after accusing Tehran's Revolutionary Guards of orchestrating the October sabotage. rumours</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261110-macrons-file-new-defamation-lawsuit-against-us-podcaster-over-transgender-rumours</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte filed a second lawsuit against US right-wing podcaster Candace Owens over false claims on her gender, accusing her of continuing to spread the allegations and profiting from them despite earlier legal action. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef3af00a-dcbf-11f1-b34e-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/cb700a478b2bb0246e753a3e44c0a699e13978e9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef3af00a-dcbf-11f1-b34e-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/cb700a478b2bb0246e753a3e44c0a699e13978e9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">efe09190-dcbf-11f1-9487-5f60e87d1ec6</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 04:33:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef3af00a-dcbf-11f1-b34e-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/cb700a478b2bb0246e753a3e44c0a699e13978e9.jpg">© Abdul Saboor, POOL/AFP/File</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Top contemporary French artist Christian Boltanski dies aged 76</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210714-top-contemporary-french-artist-christian-boltanski-dies-aged-76</link><description>
Christian Boltanski, one of France's top contemporary artists whose multimedia works probed the meaning of mortality and memory, has died aged 76, a former museum director told AFP on Sunday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b7135ce8-e4c8-11eb-89be-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 18:44:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg">© Miguel Riopa, AFP</source><dc:creator>NEWS WIRES</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'Crumbs': French PM's 1.6% minimum wage increase fails to placate unions</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-french-pm-lecornu-announces-increase-minimum-wage-bid-to-calm-protests</link><description>
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday that a planned 1.6% increase in the minimum wage would be brought forward from January to December after holding talks with trade unions and business leaders over the cost-of-living crisis that has fuelled weeks of unrest across France. The increase fell well short of the demands of unions, which have called for fresh protests in the coming days.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f6ee1d4e-dc43-11f1-9280-633626f68692</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:52:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Paris police officers go on trial over 2020 beating of Black man</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-paris-police-officers-go-on-trial-over-2020-beating-of-black-man</link><description>
Three French police officers went on trial Monday over the 2020 beating of Black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris. The assault, which was captured on camera, sparked nationwide outrage and renewed scrutiny of police violence and racism in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">476e3e4a-dc24-11f1-9f04-f3d8b2b0702c</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:08:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg">© Thomas Samson, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French students vow to continue protests despite concessions from Macron govt</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261026-macron-vows-concrete-measures-to-address-student-demands-after-unrest</link><description>
French student leaders on Monday called for more protests despite President Emmanuel Macron's pledge of  "concrete and strong" measures to address their demands after weeks of nationwide unrest. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu met with high school representatives alongside education ministers to announce follow-up action ranging from a total overhaul of higher education admissions platform Parcoursup to a cap on class sizes.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ade564d2-d134-11f1-9bc8-6d20ccb9a352</guid><pubDate>Mon, 26 Oct 2026 12:25:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg">© Aurelien Morissard, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Focus</category><title>How the French army trains for 'high-intensity' combat</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/focus/20210714-how-the-french-army-trains-for-high-intensity-conflict</link><description>
France's new military programming law increases the country's defence budget to 2 percent of GDP by 2025. It's an investment in the modernisation of equipment, but also in the training of soldiers. The aim is to teach soldiers to face an army at least as well equipped as that of France in a context of global rearmament. Our reporters Fadile Bhayat, Mandi Heshmati and Caroline Grandjean followed French troops during a "high-intensity" training exercise.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">023ce07e-e41d-11eb-a94a-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 14:42:34 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Fadile BHAYAT</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says 'racist terrorist attack’ in Trappes marks turning point for France</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261023-french-prosecutors-investigate-paris-shooting-as-suspected-terror-attack</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron described Friday’s drive-by shooting in the western suburb of Trappes as a “terrorist and racist attack”, saying it marks a turning point for France. One person was killed and at least four people, including a 12-year-old girl, were wounded in the shooting, apparently at random. Two of the victims have immigrant backgrounds.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">72670cfa-ced0-11f1-8bc7-bb90dbb6a8a1</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:08:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg">© Hannah McKay, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Perspective</category><title>'A lot of French politicians are out of touch with a large part of the population'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/perspective/20220209-a-lot-of-french-politicians-are-out-of-touch-with-a-large-part-of-the-population</link><description>

He gives us his take on the French presidential election campaign, as seen from the suburbs.

French President Emmanuel Macron took aim at world leaders including US President Donald Trump for trying to exploit the riots and looting that broke out alongside peaceful demonstrations in France Saturday for their own political advantage. </description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2c665312-cd42-11f1-8dbc-290623bfb92e</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:48:11 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg">© Benoit Tessier, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'Tefal campaign': with Covid-19 monopolising voters' minds, nothing sticks</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20220209-tefal-campaign-pandemic-prudent-president-keep-french-election-race-on-the-backburner</link><description>

Two teaching staff were shot and wounded by a 14-year-old boy armed with a hunting rifle at a school in Aubagne near Marseille Monday morning, French Education Minister ‌Édouard Geffray said. Authorities said the teenager's father had been taken into custody and that there did not seem to be any link to the student protests that have swept across the country in recent weeks.

A fire "completely destroyed" Paris's historic Marché Couvert des Enfants Rouges early Monday, authorities said. The cause of the fire that swept through the capital's oldest covered food market remains unknown.

French teenagers on Tuesday clashed with police as they kept up a blockade of high schools in cities across the country to demand better conditions and more teacher hirings. The escalating standoff came as unions staged a day of demonstrations against a cost-cutting budget drafted by Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu's embattled government.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b23ed102-bbeb-11f1-861d-cf265369200f</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:53:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg">© Sameer Al-Doumy, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Legion of Honour: Police investigate corruption claims for France’s top award</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-legion-of-honour-police-investigate-corruption-claims-for-france-s-top-award</link><description>
French police took a top general into custody last week as part of an ongoing probe into potential bribery among the selection committee for the country’s highest decoration, the Legion of Honour. Investigations centre on possible payoffs for awards including expensive meals, holidays and thousands of euros in cash.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cf7e5750-bc0f-11f1-9d67-9d40f7c16032</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:43:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg">© Francois Mori, AP</source><dc:creator>Joanna YORK</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Eiffel Tower chief to step down over removal of women staff during Hindu group's visit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-eiffel-tower-chief-to-step-down-over-removal-of-women-staff-during-hindu-group-visit-baps</link><description>
The head of the Eiffel Tower is set to step down in the wake of a controversy sparked by the removal of female workers during a private visit of the Paris landmark by members of the Hindu sect BAPS, which triggered a staff walkout earlier this month and sparked outrage in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b85f821e-bc10-11f1-89fe-7b0f1abdd3bc</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:22:29 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France's Le Pen vows to 'counterattack' after top ally Bardella hit by anti-Semitism claims</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-france-s-le-pen-vows-to-counterattack-after-top-ally-bardella-hit-by-anti-semitism-claims</link><description>
French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen on Tuesday denounced an attempt to "derail" her Élysée Palace run after a media report accused the head of her far-right National Rally (RN) party, Jordan Bardella, of making ant-Semitic comments in 2013. French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents.

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The latest information, news and events in France, Europe and around the world.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:35:38 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>France requests arrest warrants for Iranian suspects over supermarket cyberattack</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261111-france-requests-arrest-warrants-for-iranian-suspects-over-supermarket-cyberattack</link><description>
France has requested international arrest warrants for three Iranian men over October’s cyberattack on supermarket fridges, while Tehran rejects the allegations as “baseless and malicious”. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a5408b50-dcf0-11f1-b997-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-29T100226Z-1803060916-RC2Q1OAGCX8L-RTRMADP-3-USA-MILITARY-FREEZERS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a5408b50-dcf0-11f1-b997-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-29T100226Z-1803060916-RC2Q1OAGCX8L-RTRMADP-3-USA-MILITARY-FREEZERS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8a8f8ab4-ddcb-11f1-8b47-cfca036f86fe</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 16:00:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a5408b50-dcf0-11f1-b997-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-29T100226Z-1803060916-RC2Q1OAGCX8L-RTRMADP-3-USA-MILITARY-FREEZERS.jpg">© Stephane Mahe/Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race vowing to expel unemployed foreigners</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261111-zemmour-joins-2027-race-vowing-to-expel-jobless-foreigners</link><description>
Far-right politician Eric Zemmour has formally entered next year’s French presidential race. He is promising a sharp cut in immigration, and the expulsion of foreigners who are out of work, even if they live in France legally.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/75824288-ddc6-11f1-b11b-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-c87e2bl.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/75824288-ddc6-11f1-b11b-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-c87e2bl.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">e4ed6918-ddc6-11f1-ab44-f53e2031ebff</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 12:55:43 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/75824288-ddc6-11f1-b11b-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-c87e2bl.jpg">© SIMON WOHLFAHRT / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Emmanuel and Brigitte Macron file new lawsuit in US against right-wing influencer</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261111-emmanuel-and-brigitte-macron-file-new-lawsuit-in-us-against-right-wing-influencer</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte have filed a new defamation lawsuit in the United States against conservative influencer Candace Owens, who claims the French First Lady is a transgender woman.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c32c0b32-dcf8-11f1-9d6d-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26281300022948.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c32c0b32-dcf8-11f1-9d6d-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26281300022948.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">e1014d56-dcf9-11f1-b466-e9d2e52e2a56</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:59:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c32c0b32-dcf8-11f1-9d6d-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26281300022948.jpg">© Abdul Saboor/Reuters pool via AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Teachers divided over compulsory 11 November ceremonies at schools</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261111-teachers-divided-over-compulsory-11-november-ceremonies-at-schools</link><description>
A new government initiative requires primary schools across France to hold ceremonies honouring those who died for the country. But teachers are divided over its purpose and the role of the military in education.

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8c795750-c2d3-11f1-9d03-c55799ef8309/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D2DV9WP.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8c795750-c2d3-11f1-9d03-c55799ef8309/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D2DV9WP.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">94610092-d8ec-11f1-83cc-05d8d1a87801</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 08:19:33 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8c795750-c2d3-11f1-9d03-c55799ef8309/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D2DV9WP.jpg">© AFP/Dimitar Dilkoff</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Mass protests sweep France as workers and students demand higher pay and funding</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261105-french-unions-join-forces-for-nationwide-strike-as-protests-intensify</link><description>
Hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets across France on Thursday as workers, students and pensioners joined nationwide strikes and demonstrations demanding higher wages, action on the cost of living and better public services. Nearly 1.6 million people joined the marches, including 350,000 in Paris, the CGT union said. The Interior Ministry gave a much lower nationwide estimate of around 600,000.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3e9309cc-d936-11f1-b338-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26309546527183.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3e9309cc-d936-11f1-b338-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26309546527183.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d1ac4db2-d847-11f1-8e8e-b39696b484d3</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 07:11:27 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3e9309cc-d936-11f1-b338-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26309546527183.jpg">© AP Photo/Thibault Camus</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Students blockade dozens of high schools in France before nationwide strike</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261103-students-blockade-dozens-of-high-schools-in-france-before-nationwide-strike</link><description>
Students blockaded dozens of high schools across France on Tuesday to maintain pressure on the government over education reforms as trade unions prepared for a nationwide strike later this week.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/21c9ae56-d6d2-11f1-afea-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D64N373.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/21c9ae56-d6d2-11f1-afea-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D64N373.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f797ebc-d75d-11f1-9716-917a4357a158</guid><pubDate>Tue, 03 Nov 2026 12:20:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/21c9ae56-d6d2-11f1-afea-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D64N373.jpg">© Matthieu Rondel / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Calls mount to ban French TV channel following racist killing</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261102-calls-mount-to-ban-french-tv-channel-after-racist-killing</link><description>

      <title>College students rally in support of Starbucks baristas urging boycott over contract impasse</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/12/starbucks-workers-campus-rally-contract-talks</link>
      <description><p>Rallies take place on more than US 40 campuses as workers seeking better pay and conditions decry stalled talks</p><p>Starbucks baristas, students, elected officials and allies are holding rallies at <a href="https://starbucksworkersunited.controlshift.app/events?link_id=2&amp;can_id=debd8d2ad19f005d15f9bbdff314d42a&amp;source=email-nov-12-day-of-action-for-starbucks-baristas&amp;email_referrer=email_3490793&amp;email_subject=nov-12-day-of-action-for-starbucks-baristas&amp;&amp;">over 40 college campuses</a> across the US on Thursday to support the Starbucks Workers United <a href="https://www.boycottstarbucks.net/">boycott campaign</a> as the union nears five years of deadlock with the company over contract negotiations.</p><p>Starbucks Workers United is <a href="https://sbworkersunited.org/what-were-fighting-for-updates-on-contract-bargaining/">seeking</a> better pay and stronger staffing levels, including a $17 an hour minimum wage for baristas and a minimum staffing of three workers per store. It has called on the public to <a href="https://www.boycottstarbucks.net/">boycott</a> Starbucks until its first contract is reached.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/12/starbucks-workers-campus-rally-contract-talks">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Home sales hit 16-year low in October amid record-high mortgage rates</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/12/home-sales-october-low</link>
      <description><p>Sales of built units fell to 3.75m in October, down by 8.8% from last year, with mortgage rates at nearly three-year high</p><p>US existing home sales hit a 16-year low in October as buyers were driven away by record-high <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/money/mortgage-rates">mortgage rates</a> and rising inflation, according to new data released on Wednesday.</p><p>Sales of already built units dropped to 3.75m in October, down by 8.8% from last year, the National Association of Realtors (NAR) reported. The median existing-home sales price increased slightly to $416,700. Declines in sales were seen in the midwest, south and west, though sales in the north-east held steady.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/12/home-sales-october-low">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Democrats’ US election sweep brings the price of their promised social contract into focus</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/11/democrats-election-medicaid-costs</link>
      <description><p>‘The post-election wish list is about to run into harsh fiscal reality: there is no money’</p><p>Is this an opportunity for a new America? As the Reagan revolution four decades ago launched US society down the path to low taxes and meager solidarity, perhaps the Republican bloodbath last week could turn US politics toward building a new social contract anchored on an aspiration to equitable prosperity.</p><p>One can sense the ambition of the bumper new crop of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/democrats">Democrats</a> ushered to power last week, calling for support for programs for children and their parents; emphatically endorsing the long-held dream of Medicare for All. The project includes rolling back <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/donaldtrump">Donald Trump</a>’s cuts to Medicaid and food stamps, and restoring subsidies for health insurance under the Affordable Care Act that Republicans allowed to expire. And that’s just the start.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/11/democrats-election-medicaid-costs">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Federal judge allows Trump’s $10bn defamation lawsuit against BBC to proceed</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/10/trump-10bn-defamation-lawsuit-bbc-allowed</link>
      <description><p>Trump-appointed judge Jeffrey T Kuntz partially denies British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss over edit</p><p>Federal judge Jeffrey T Kuntz ruled on Tuesday that Donald Trump’s lawsuit against the BBC can proceed, denying in part the British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss the case. The president’s $10bn defamation lawsuit stems from the BBC’s splicing together of disparate comments he made before the 6 January US Capitol insurrection, as rendered in a Panorama documentary called Trump: A Second Chance.</p><p>“Accepting the allegations in the complaint as true, the Court finds Trump plausibly pled damages where Trump alleges a defamatory documentary released toward the election caused reputational harm,” the Trump-appointed Florida district court judge wrote. “It would be difficult for the Court to accept a different framing without completely negating the significance and fragility of political elections.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/10/trump-10bn-defamation-lawsuit-bbc-allowed">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>New data comes after Republicans’ midterms losses – which were largely seen as a rebuke of the party over high prices</p><p>US inflation rose 0.4% from September to October, slightly above expectations but still a cooldown in price increases as the cost of gas dipped during the month.</p><p>The Bureau of Labor Statistics did not release the usual year-over-year inflation figure as part of the consumer price index (CPI), which measures the price of a basket of goods and services, as data was not collected in October 2025 during the government shutdown.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/10/october-inflation-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>California lawsuit comes as Donald Trump says FBI is investigating tech CEO’s links with Alice Huang</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/09/nvidia-board-jensen-huang">Nvidia’s board needs to do some succession planning – sharpish</a></p></li></ul><p>Nvidia and its chief executive, Jensen Huang, have been accused of misleading shareholders in a lawsuit over the Chinese <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/09/nvidia-jensen-huang-us-china-donald-trump-spy">spying scandal</a> engulfing the $4.3tn (£3.2tn) company.</p><p>The legal action came as Donald Trump <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/video/2026/nov/09/trump-hegseth-jensen-huang">said the FBI was investigating Huang’s affair</a> with an alleged Chinese spy.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/10/nvidia-jensen-huang-sued-donald-trump-fbi">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Brent crude drops below $90 and markets climb after president downplays prospect of further strikes</p><p>Oil prices have fallen to the lowest level since late August while stock markets climbed higher, as markets reacted with relief to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/09/trump-iran-war">Donald Trump saying that the war on Iran is “effectively over”</a>.</p><p>Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, fell nearly 3% to $89.66, the lowest since 31 August, on Tuesday morning, after the US president downplayed the need for military action against Iran “at this point”.       <title>Farewell to Elon Musk’s Cybertruck. Has any car ever been more repellent? | Arwa Mahdawi</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/11/farewell-cybertruck-elon-musk-car-repellent</link>
      <description><p>Safety campaigners have condemned it and owners have complained about it. Goodbye to a steel monstrosity seemingly designed by a five-year-old</p><p>Elon Musk is having a rough go of it, isn’t he? The world’s richest man spent almost half a billion dollars on the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/04/elon-musk-midterm-spending-analysis">midterms</a> in a failed attempt to defend Republican control of government. Now the tech mogul, who moved from California to Texas to escape Democrats and regulations, finds himself in a newly blue state. He also finds himself the subject of an unflattering <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/sep/08/musk-review-epic-study-worlds-richest-most-banal-man-elon-film">documentary</a> and, if the Democrats follow through on threats to investigate him, could potentially be in a spot of legal bother.</p><p>And to top it all off? Musk’s beloved Cybertruck, the steel monstrosity that looks as if it were designed by a five-year-old, is <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/06/tesla-to-wind-down-cybertruck-production-as-elon-musk-focuses-on-robotics-and-ai">winding down production</a>. According to Musk, this isn’t because it’s an abject failure, but because he is channelling his energy into other things. “This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media,” Musk <a href="https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2119691615774146614?a=pN3ISFVZZ-aU4_-TlJw&amp;s=20">tweeted</a> on Monday. “But rather that the opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production.” (The Cybercab is a two-passenger robotaxi.)</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/11/farewell-cybertruck-elon-musk-car-repellent">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Farmers face big drop in production from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event</p><p>Banana producers in Latin America are calling for better pay to help cope with the impact of the climate crisis, as they face big drops in production resulting from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event.</p><p>High winds in parts of Colombia, one of the biggest suppliers to the UK market where droughts are predicted in some regions this year, and heavy rainfall in Peru and Ecuador are already affecting production, according to the Fairtrade Foundation ethical trade body.       <description><p>A layoff and a leap of faith convinced Katie Teixeira she had what it takes to run her own business</p><p>In 2010, Katie Teixeira adopted a kitten found all alone in an abandoned house.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/12/michael-carrick-manchester-united-sacked</link>
      <description><p>Disastrous decisions and confused appointments have been a constant theme at Old Trafford since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement in 2013</p><p>For a window into the alarming dysfunction at Manchester United that Michael Carrick failed to manage and <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/12/michael-carrick-sacked-manchester-united-mauricio-pochettino">caused his sacking</a>, consider the case of Eddie Howe, initially a favourite to succeed the 45-year-old before Mauricio Pochettino’s emergence as the chosen one.</p><p>The former Newcastle manager had been Jason Wilcox’s choice to take over from Carrick. Howe was also the favoured candidate of Dan Ashworth, Wilcox’s predecessor as United’s director of football, to follow Erik ten Hag after the Dutchman’s sacking in October 2024.       <description><ul><li><p>USSF cites state department advisory about Qatar</p></li><li><p>Competition set to kick off in eight days</p></li></ul><p>The US men’s national team have pulled out of the Fifa U-17 World Cup, which is due to kick off in Qatar in just over a week. In a letter sent to players explaining the decision, the US Soccer Federation cited safety concerns for players and staff, referring them to the <a href="https://travel.state.gov/en/international-travel/travel-advisories/qatar.html">US state department’s travel advisory</a> for Qatar, which encourages citizens to reconsider travel to the country “due to risk of armed conflict” and asks government employees to obtain special authorization to do so.</p><p>“Unfortunately, in light of current circumstances … we are no longer able to participate in the tournament,” US Soccer’s letter to players reads. “The wellbeing of our players and staff will always be our top priority.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/11/usa-u-17-world-cup-qatar-withdrawal-middle-east-conflict">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Is No 10 still the best, or No 41? The myths and maths of Premier League shirt numbers</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/11/is-no-10-still-the-best-or-no-41-the-myths-and-maths-of-premier-league-shirt-numbers</link>
      <description><p>While No 9s still score the most goals and No 1s try to stop them, trends have changed since the introduction of squad numbers in the early 1990s</p><p>How much is a shirt number worth? It costs £8 if you want two digits added to the back of Arsenal’s 2026-27 home shirt, whereas Manchester City add on £16 for customisation, whether you want a name as well as a number or not.</p><p>That is cheap compared to what baseball players decide among themselves. Juan Soto bought Brett Baty a $92,000 (£69,000) car in exchange for getting his preferred number (22) when he joined the New York Mets last year. But that’s baseball, where they allow players to wear ‘0’. Anything goes.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/11/is-no-10-still-the-best-or-no-41-the-myths-and-maths-of-premier-league-shirt-numbers">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Michael Carrick’s replacement must find solutions on the pitch and pressure the hierarchy to accept a share of blame</p><p>One of the final images of Michael Carrick’s time in charge will be of him standing in the rain on the Old Trafford touchline <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/25/manchester-united-bournemouth-premier-league-match-report-michael-carrick">watching his side succumb to Bournemouth</a>, while his sullen captain sat unused on the bench. Bruno Fernandes was dropped after calling out his head coach’s tactics, although Carrick said it was for football reasons.       <description><p>Who is football’s most legendary No 9? Has there ever been a legendary No 28? And why exactly does Mario Balotelli love wearing No 45 so much? Here’s our list and the stories behind it</p><p>The relationship between players and numbers is a long-established one filled with memories and fascinating as well as fun stories behind them. With that in mind, the Guardian has had a go at deciding which male player is best associated with each squad number, from 1-50.       <title>Complaint filed to IRS in relation to Fifa head Gianni Infantino’s housekeeper</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/11/complaint-us-irs-fifa-gianni-infantino-housekeeper</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>It calls for inquiry into claims she was on Fifa payroll</p></li><li><p>Fifa: Infantino personally pays for ‘any domestic staff’</p></li></ul><p>A complaint has been filed to the United States Internal Revenue Service calling for an investigation into claims an individual on the Fifa payroll was working privately as a housekeeper for Gianni Infantino.</p><p>If the IRS investigates and finds the claims to be proven then Fifa could lose its tax-exempt status in the US.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/11/thomas-tuchel-unfinished-business-england-euro-2028-nations-league</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Head coach did not insert release clause into contract</p></li><li><p>Tuchel ‘open to everything’ including staying after Euros</p></li></ul><p>Thomas Tuchel will not be going anywhere before Euro 2028. Mauricio Pochettino is expected to leave his role as the USA men’s head coach to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/11/manchester-united-close-mauricio-pochettino-deal-michael-carrick">replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United</a>, but Tuchel has not lost his passion for international football and has revealed he did not insert a release clause when he extended his deal as England’s manager this year.</p><p>It will not matter whether there is an approach from a big club before the next tournament. United can pay about £7m to get Pochettino out of his deal, but the Football Association does not have to worry about being forced to let Tuchel go. “There’s no intention [of leaving],” Tuchel said. “I signed the contract. I want to stay until the Euros. I want to do the Euros. We have unfinished business.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/11/thomas-tuchel-unfinished-business-england-euro-2028-nations-league">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Which football club has had most international captains in the same team? | The Knowledge</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/11/football-club-most-international-captains-same-team-the-knowledge</link>
      <description><p>Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers</p><ul><li><p><a href="mailto:knowledge@theguardian.com"><strong>Mail us</strong></a><strong> with all of your questions and answers</strong></p></li></ul><p><strong>“Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?”</strong> asks MH Zahid. <strong>“Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?”</strong></p><p>A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at <em>that</em> time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/11/football-club-most-international-captains-same-team-the-knowledge">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Obsessive attention to detail is helping striker to reach new heights – and a 126th international appearance on Thursday</p><p>It was Harry Kane’s dirty little secret. Something the England captain got up to after&nbsp;matches. He felt he deserved the indulgence. Yes,&nbsp;it can be revealed, Kane loved to reward himself after a gruelling 90 minutes with a bag of sweets. “I do like a Haribo,” he said with a smile after the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/sep/29/czechia-england-nations-league-match-report">Nations&nbsp;League win against Czechia</a> in Prague at the end of September.</p><p>No more. At the beginning of last&nbsp;season, Kane took the decision to cut out the naughty treats. After&nbsp;a while, he noticed a difference.     <item>
      <title>From W-M to the No 10, shirt numbers tell a story of football’s tactical evolution</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/10/shirt-numbers-tell-story-football-tactical-evolution</link>
      <description><p>In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, as well as the attributes a player was supposed to demonstrate</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/ng-interactive/2026/nov/10/ultimate-1-50-the-male-footballers-best-associated-with-each-squad-number">Ultimate 1-50: check out our complete list of players</a></p></li></ul><p>Numbers have a fascination. The No 10 is revered almost everywhere, but perhaps most especially in Argentina, where it denotes the playmaker, the <em>enganche</em>, the quasi-mythical figure who links the front and back of the team. Liverpool and Manchester United have reasons to celebrate their No 7. Ajax retired No 14 for Johan Cruyff, Milan their No 3 and No 6 for Paolo Maldini and Franco Baresi respectively and Birmingham their 22 for Jude Bellingham as gestures of respect for their abilities. Other numbers have been retired to mark premature deaths: the No 20 at Liverpool for Diogo Jota, the No 23 at Manchester City for Marc-Vivian Foé, the 21 at Espanyol for Daniel Jarque.</p><p>But numbers are not just about individuals. In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, and the expectations of particular numbers in particular cultures, as well as the attributes a player in that shirt was supposed to demonstrate, themselves tell a story of tactical evolution.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/10/shirt-numbers-tell-story-football-tactical-evolution">Continue reading...</a></description>

Le leader de LFI et candidat à l'élection présidentielle en France, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, a reçu l'interdiction d'entrer en Israël, a fait savoir le ministère israélien des Affaires étrangères, accusant La France insoumise de tenir une "position extrêmement hostile à Israël".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/33654616-dab0-11f1-ad25-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-14T100614Z-1152484815-RC2Y2OATJ5N2-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/33654616-dab0-11f1-ad25-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-14T100614Z-1152484815-RC2Y2OATJ5N2-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0d8879d4-debd-11f1-acfd-a78d57209718</guid><pubDate>Thu, 12 Nov 2026 17:25:25 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/33654616-dab0-11f1-ad25-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-14T100614Z-1152484815-RC2Y2OATJ5N2-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS.jpg">© Reuters, Abdul Saboor</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Élément Terre, la quotidienne</category><title>COP31: Le Népal, martyr du climat, en quête de réparations</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/%C3%A9l%C3%A9ment-terre-la-quotidienne/20261112-cop31-le-n%C3%A9pal-martyr-du-climat-en-qu%C3%AAte-de-r%C3%A9parations</link><description>
Le Népal a subit 2 catastrophes climatiques juste avant la COP31 qui ont fait des milliers de morts et de disparus. Pour la première fois, le fond pertes et dommages a promis une aide d'urgence mais elle tarde à être versée et ne couvrirait qu'une infime part des besoins de reconstruction. </description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3bee9654-dea5-11f1-b354-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261112-150145-150322-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3bee9654-dea5-11f1-b354-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261112-150145-150322-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4115cf62-dea5-11f1-a0a0-b991e5bb2949</guid><pubDate>Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:25:02 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Guerre en Ukraine : les émissaires américains affirment "des libérations de prisonniers"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261112-guerre-en-ukraine-les-%C3%A9missaires-am%C3%A9ricains-affirment-des-lib%C3%A9rations-de-prisonniers</link><description>
Lors d'une entrevue au Kremlin le jeudi 12 novembre, les émissaires américains Jared Kushner et Steve Witkoff ont exhorté le président russe à intégrer les pays européens aux pourparlers destinés à mettre un terme à la guerre en Ukraine. Lors de cette rencontre, Jared Kushner a affirmé que les négociations ont mené "aux plus grandes libérations humanitaires de prisonniers.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/127a3a12-dea5-11f1-ad00-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261112-150345-150525-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/127a3a12-dea5-11f1-ad00-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261112-150345-150525-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">185ec934-dea5-11f1-a448-d3954c934f42</guid><pubDate>Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:21:17 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Narchomicide en France : perpétuité requise contre quatre accusés</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261112-france-perp%C3%A9tuit%C3%A9-requise-contre-quatre-accus%C3%A9s-dont-deux-barons-de-la-drogue</link><description>
Dénonçant la "barbarie poussée à l'extrême" d'un triple narchomicide dont l'une des victimes est le frère d'Amine Kessaci, figure de la lutte anti-narcotrafic, l'accusation a requis mercredi 11 novembre la réclusion à perpétuité pour quatre des cinq co-accusés, dont deux figures du narcobanditisme marseillais. Les explications de Marie Schuster, journaliste à France 24.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c0138ba8-dea3-11f1-9d2a-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261112-142146-142738-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c0138ba8-dea3-11f1-9d2a-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261112-142146-142738-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c554b092-dea3-11f1-a7bd-2b7a8fc97421</guid><pubDate>Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:17:47 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Présidentielle 2027 : le "Made in France", un enjeu devenu majeur dans la campagne</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261112-france-presidentielle-2027-le-made-in-france-un-enjeu-devenu-majeur-dans-la-campagne</link><description>
Le salon du "Made in France", qui se tient du 12 au 15 novembre à Paris, verra défiler de nombreux candidats à l’élection présidentielle française. Ceux-ci ont conscience qu’il s’agit d’un levier pour relancer l’économie française, mais aussi de l’importance de cet enjeu auprès des électeurs.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/daba36b6-deab-11f1-aca2-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/main-made-in-france.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/daba36b6-deab-11f1-aca2-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/main-made-in-france.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ed1d7990-de9b-11f1-95c5-dfbb75da96b1</guid><pubDate>Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:15:33 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/daba36b6-deab-11f1-aca2-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/main-made-in-france.png">© AFP / Studio graphique, FMM</source><dc:creator>Romain BRUNET</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>France : des appels au meurtre de livreurs étrangers, un système d'entraide se met en place</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261112-france-des-appels-au-meurtre-de-livreurs-%C3%A9trangers-un-syst%C3%A8me-d-entraide-se-met-en-place</link><description>
Alors que des appels à agresser et à tuer des livreurs étrangers ont été diffusés sur les réseaux sociaux par des extrémistes, la peur s'est installée chez ces travailleurs précaires, dont beaucoup sont en situation irrégulière. En l'absence de mesures concrètes mises en place par les plateformes de livraison pour les protéger, un système d'entraide tente de se mettre en place chez les acteurs du secteur. Les explications de Leslie Carretero, journaliste à InfoMigrants.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3a55267e-dea4-11f1-a6de-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261112-143042-143812-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3a55267e-dea4-11f1-a6de-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261112-143042-143812-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">3fcfb7a4-dea4-11f1-ae5d-532d90dac80a</guid><pubDate>Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:14:18 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Midterms 2026 : exploit des démocrates dans le Mississippi avec l'élection de Scott Colom</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261112-midterms-2026-exploit-des-d%C3%A9mocrates-dans-le-mississippi-avec-l-%C3%A9lection-de-scott-colom</link><description>
Le démocrate Scott Colom est crédité d'une victoire historique dans le Mississippi face à la sénatrice ​républicaine sortante Cindy Hyde-Smith lors des élections de mi-mandat au Congrès américain ce mercredi 11 novembre. Scott Colom devient le premier afro-américain élu sénateur dans cet ​Etat du ‌sud du pays depuis un siècle et demi. Il est également ⁠le premier démocrate à y remporter un siège au Sénat depuis John Stennis en 1982. Les explications de Sylvain Rousseau, journaliste à France 24.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ed8042f8-dea2-11f1-87e5-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261112-141415-142145-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ed8042f8-dea2-11f1-87e5-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261112-141415-142145-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f39050a2-dea2-11f1-a1c2-037f07c00b13</guid><pubDate>Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:11:14 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

En France, 68 projets de data centers sont en cours selon les observatoires spécialisés, bien qu'un collectif d'opposant en ait décompté 110. Ces énormes centres de données utilisés surtout pour l'intelligence artificielle, sont déjà plus de 300 en France et leur présence suscite de plus en plus d'opposition, à cause du bruit et l'impact sur l'écologie.

Cela fait 500 jours que le journaliste français Christophe Gleizes est détenu en Algérie. Ses parents ont confié à France 24 leurs inquiétudes et leurs espoirs.
 
"500 jours, c'est énorme pour nous et c'est très cruel. Il y a eu quelques ouvertures avec le début du réchauffement diplomatique entre la France et l'Algérie. Il y a eu aussi la visite du pape en Algérie, la FIFA qui a accrédité Christophe pour le mondial et puis au final rien ne s'est passé. De nouveau, on comprend que la relation entre Alger et Paris, n'est plus vraiment une très bonne relation. C'est très tendu et ça nous inquiète énormément".
 
Le ministre français des Affaires étrangères, Jean-Noël Barrot, a reçu mercredi au Quai d'Orsay la mère, le beau-père et le frère du journaliste.
 
"On compte sur notre diplomatie pour agir diplomatiquement parce qu'il est clair que nous ne cherchons pas de provocation vis-à-vis du gouvernement algérien. On lui demande simplement d'accorder la grâce à Christophe. Nous sommes absolument hostiles à toute montée en tension. Bien au contraire, on a toujours été pour l'apaisement, mais il faudrait quand même qu'on nous entende", ont-ils déclaré sur notre antenne.
 
Retrouvez l'intégralité de l'entretien dans la vidéo ci-dessus.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/885b46d4-dddf-11f1-b4d5-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261111-153000-153959-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/885b46d4-dddf-11f1-b4d5-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261111-153000-153959-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8da077ea-dddf-11f1-9a48-ad5ab2952c35</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 14:59:46 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Bruno Retailleau propose une primaire de la droite et du centre les 31 janvier et 7 février</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261111-bruno-retailleau-propose-une-primaire-de-la-droite-et-du-centre-les-31-janvier-et-7-f%C3%A9vrier</link><description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8ddf9566-ddd4-11f1-a864-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261111-133146-134545-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8ddf9566-ddd4-11f1-a864-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261111-133146-134545-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">92c3555e-ddd4-11f1-be46-e35a5801da9e</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 13:45:16 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Commémorations de l'Armistice du 11-Novembre : "un devoir de mémoire"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261111-comm%C3%A9morations-de-l-armistice-du-11-novembre-un-devoir-de-m%C3%A9moire</link><description>
Guillaume Ancel, ancien officier, chroniqueur et co-auteur de "Les faussaires de la nation" (éditions Phillipe Rey), était l'invité de l'antenne de France 24.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9f0eaef6-ddcc-11f1-b848-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261111-130131-132550-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9f0eaef6-ddcc-11f1-b848-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261111-130131-132550-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a4798b04-ddcc-11f1-999a-abafb223025a</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 13:25:10 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Un match solidaire pour la libération de Christophe Gleizes, détenu depuis 500 jours</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261111-un-match-solidaire-pour-la-lib%C3%A9ration-de-christophe-gleizes-d%C3%A9tenu-depuis-500-jours</link><description>
Un match solidaire, organisé par Reporters sans frontières (RSF) avec la Ville de Paris et réunissant des personnalités du football, des médias et de la culture, est prévu mercredi soir pour appeler à libérer Christophe Gleizes, emprisonné en Algérie depuis 500 jours.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/62ac1ef8-ddc7-11f1-955d-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261111-121223-121423-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/62ac1ef8-ddc7-11f1-955d-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261111-121223-121423-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">67548a4e-ddc7-11f1-8a92-bd99fe73a29c</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 12:07:09 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Discriminations : ils lancent une marche anti-raciste à travers la France</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261111-discriminations-ils-lancent-une-marche-anti-raciste-%C3%A0-travers-la-france</link><description>
Après l'attentat raciste survenu à Trappes et La Verrière le 23 octobre, une marche nationale contre le racisme et les discours de haine veut relier Marseille aux villes de Trappes et La Verrière. 
 
Lancée par des citoyens depuis la petite ville de Millau dans l'Aveyron, cette initiative entend faire revivre les symboles de la Marche pour l'égalité et contre le racisme de 1983.  En pleine organisation, les initiateurs espèrent mobiliser des participants à chaque étape du parcours. La marche partira le 23 novembre de la cité phocéenne pour arriver à Trappes le 26 décembre. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0f5e914c-ddc5-11f1-93ce-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/vignette-VF-MARCHE-2026.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0f5e914c-ddc5-11f1-93ce-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/vignette-VF-MARCHE-2026.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">55b1b338-ddc3-11f1-9bb1-f7d848332d7d</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:44:06 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>La France célèbre le 108e anniversaire de l'Armistice du 11 novembre 1918</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261111-la-france-c%C3%A9l%C3%A8bre-le-108e-anniversaire-de-l-armistice-du-11-novembre-1918</link><description>
Une circulaire parue début juillet instaure une cérémonie annuelle "d'hommage à tous les 'Morts pour la France'" pour les élèves du CM1 à la terminale autour du 11-Novembre, à laquelle des élus ou des militaires pourraient participer. Dans la Loire, les collégiens se sont préparés à cet hommage. Reportage.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9b30def0-ddc0-11f1-b737-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261111-120231-120327-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9b30def0-ddc0-11f1-b737-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261111-120231-120327-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a04a3544-ddc0-11f1-a763-8b44380c7aa5</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:17:53 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>11-Novembre : ravivage de la flamme sur la tombe du soldat inconnu par Emmanuel Macron</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261111-11-novembre-ravivage-de-la-flamme-sur-la-tombe-du-soldat-inconnu-par-emmanuel-macron</link><description>
Le président français Emmanuel Macron a procédé ce mercredi au ravivage de la flamme sur la tombe du soldat inconnu à l'occasion du 108e anniversaire de l’Armistice du 11 novembre 1918.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/938cd0c2-ddbc-11f1-b050-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261111-113055-113311-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/938cd0c2-ddbc-11f1-b050-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261111-113055-113311-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">98849e5c-ddbc-11f1-854c-132fd982fa1d</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:51:12 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Triple narchomicide à Marseille en 2020 : le parquet requiert la perpétuité contre les accusés</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261111-la-perp%C3%A9tuit%C3%A9-requise-contre-quatre-accus%C3%A9s-dont-deux-barons-de-la-drogue-marseillais</link><description>
La cour d'assises d'Aix-en-Provence a requis, mercredi, la prison à perpétuité pour les deux commanditaires présumés du triple assassinat à Marseille, en 2020, dont l'une des victimes est le frère aîné du militant anti-narcotrafic Amine Kessaci. Les autres accusés risquent de lourdes peines d'emprisonnement.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/433d09ae-ddb5-11f1-a8bf-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/8f652e1c6bbb46060474f0ed45be4e0aea48b1c1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/433d09ae-ddb5-11f1-a8bf-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/8f652e1c6bbb46060474f0ed45be4e0aea48b1c1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">44310932-ddb5-11f1-beb6-47fc4dae7fcf</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:50:01 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/433d09ae-ddb5-11f1-a8bf-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/8f652e1c6bbb46060474f0ed45be4e0aea48b1c1.jpg">© Benoit Peyrucq, AFP/Archives</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Christophe Gleizes, le journaliste français en prison depuis 500 jours en Algérie</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261111-christophe-gleizes-le-journaliste-fran%C3%A7ais-en-prison-depuis-500-jours-en-alg%C3%A9rie</link><description>
Pierre De La Saussay, ami de Christophe Gleizes et membre du comité de soutien, est notre invité.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a37502a4-ddab-11f1-bf5d-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261111-080447-081122-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a37502a4-ddab-11f1-bf5d-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261111-080447-081122-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a871cb34-ddab-11f1-9994-9f8e64a5a363</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:15:06 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Emmanuel Macron préside un dernier 11-Novembre marqué par une polémique</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261111-ceremonies-du-11-novembre-une-polemique-hommage-national-education-histoire</link><description>
À l'occasion du 108e anniversaire de l’Armistice de 1918, le président Emmanuel Macron s'est rendu mercredi sur les Champs-Élysées et à l'Arc de Triomphe pour raviver la flamme du soldat inconnu. Les célébrations du 11-Novembre ont donné lieu cette année à des débats sur les commémorations organisées dans les écoles.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/73174a34-ddcb-11f1-939c-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D76A88U.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/73174a34-ddcb-11f1-939c-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D76A88U.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">26583ae8-dda1-11f1-9a4c-516860d3f83a</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:38:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/73174a34-ddcb-11f1-939c-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D76A88U.jpg">© AFP, Teresa Suarez</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>
